sections.title: 01  Current standalone ACS
sections.text: Baseline ACS owns call control and duplex audio. License checklist Reference stack: ACS number, Call Automation, Event Grid/callbacks, and media WSS feeding the Python engine. Compare component swaps . ACS architecture, call flows & runtime support The outbound helper uses an ACS source phone number and CallAutomationClient.create_call . Inbound calls arrive through Event Grid; the app answers and receives subsequent ACS callbacks directly. The media socket is a separate, bidirectional WSS path. In this implementation it carries PCM16, mono, 16 kHz ; the VoiceLive bridge handles the 24 kHz service audio boundary. Call setup and media options · VoiceLive bridge . ACS has two distinct paths into FastAPI: HTTPS call events/control and duplex WSS audio. Event Grid delivers incoming-call events, not the media stream. Text equivalent & all flow steps Inbound call A PSTN caller reaches the ACS number. ACS emits an IncomingCall event through Event Grid to the app. FastAPI answers through Call Automation. ACS callbacks report the evolving connection state. ACS opens duplex media WSS. The native Cascade or VoiceLive engine consumes audio and streams the response back. YAML agents, tools, and scenarios drive the conversation; Redis and Cosmos retain the configured session and persistence data. Outbound call The app requests create_call using an ACS-purchased source number and the selected recipient. ACS attempts the call and reports outcomes by callback. Request acceptance does not mean the recipient answered. Once connected, duplex ACS media reaches the same native engine as an inbound call. The same agent definitions, tool policy, and configured persistence apply. Human handoff The agent resolves an allowed human destination. This is a telephony transfer, not a YAML agent-to-agent handoff. The app requests the configured ACS transfer. ACS attempts a new human call leg; it is not instantaneous. Correlate success or failure callbacks. Do not tell the caller the transfer completed just because the request was accepted. Retain authorized context and apply explicit failure/cleanup policy. Context is not automatically delivered to a human desktop by the phone call. Keep Python/FastAPI, native engines, YAML registries, tool policy, Redis/Cosmos, ACS callbacks and media framing. sections.title: 02  Teams Phone via ACS / TPE
sections.text: Proposed Accelerator integration design based on public TPE documentation. License checklist Reuse the ACS bridge; add Teams identity. TPE connects a licensed resource account and service number to ACS Call Automation. The design shown here aims to retain the Python runtime, callbacks, and media protocol; that reuse must be implemented and validated. TPE architecture · GA scope . Swap: ACS source-number identity → Teams resource account. Add: TPE association and access. See what stays . Known limit: Teams → third-party agent → external-number transfer/conference is documented as failing. Exact scenario . Teams/TPE architecture, call flows & public prerequisites Proposed accelerator integration using the public TPE model, shown with Direct Routing: carrier → certified SBC → Teams Phone RA, optionally through an auto attendant/call queue → TPE/ACS → accelerator. Calling Plans and Operator Connect are alternative PSTN connectivity choices. Text equivalent & all flow steps Inbound call The carrier and certified SBC route a PSTN call into Teams Direct Routing and the configured resource-account number. The configured Teams/AA/CQ path reaches the TPE application. ACS delivers the incoming event through Event Grid. FastAPI answers with ACS Call Automation. Audio still arrives over the existing ACS duplex WSS protocol. The same Cascade or VoiceLive engine, agents, tools, and persistence serve the conversation. Outbound call The app calls ACS create_call with the Teams resource-account object ID as teams_app_source, after server-side access assignment. Teams telephony originates the PSTN leg using the RA's service identity and configured carrier route, not an ACS-purchased source number. ACS callbacks report connection or failure. Missing licensing, authorization, or route configuration must surface as errors. After connection, the reused ACS socket, engine, and session stack handle audio and context. Human handoff Resolve the destination and check the exact originating topology against the documented transfer limitations. For a supported scenario, request transfer through ACS/TPE toward the Teams or PSTN human destination. Wait for the actual outcome. The specific Teams-to-third-party-agent-to-external-number scenario below is documented as failing. If transfer fails, retain or recover the caller under a designed fallback. Share only authorized context through a separate integration. Reuse ACS Call Automation, Event Grid/callbacks, duplex media, both engines, hangup, YAML agents/tools/scenarios, Redis/Cosmos. Add Teams RA, service number, licensing, app identity, RA-to-ACS association, server access assignment, carrier route; SBC/DNS/certificates when using Direct Routing. Replace, not remove Replace the ACS-purchased source-number assumption with Teams RA identity. Do not remove ACS control or media.

sections.title: 03  ACS-independent Graph calling bot
sections.text: Proposed New calling bot, media host, and bridge. License checklist Keep Python behind a Windows/.NET media service. Graph controls calls, including documented PSTN scenarios; its REST API does not stream PCM. Graph v1.0 calling · Media requirements . Swap: ACS control/media → Graph call control + Windows/.NET media. Add: a custom Python bridge. See the component mapping . Support gate: Graph REST is v1.0; the separate real-time media platform page still says developer preview. This is not a Linux-only drop-in. Graph architecture, call flows & media-host requirements Graph HTTPS controls calls; the separate .NET real-time media SDK receives/injects audio. New bot, affinity, and bridge components sit in front of the retained Python runtime. No ACS node is part of this proposed path. Text equivalent & all flow steps Inbound call A supported Teams/PSTN call reaches the bot's application instance. Graph delivers the incoming-call notification to its registered callback. The bot answers with the appropriate permissions and application-hosted media configuration; pin the call to its media instance. The Windows/.NET media SDK handles audio. A newly engineered duplex bridge exchanges it with Python, not through Graph REST. Retain the native engine and business definitions; map identities, formats, backpressure, interruption, and lifecycle explicitly. Outbound call Custom orchestration asks the bot service to create a Graph call using an authorized application identity. A provisioned, numbered application instance can originate documented PSTN scenarios; Graph is not limited to internal Teams calls. Track asynchronous call state and the chosen media host. A successful API response is not proof the destination answered. After connection, the .NET media leg and custom bridge carry audio to/from the retained AI runtime. Human handoff Resolve destination identity and tenant/number constraints; pass a correlated transfer request to the bot service. Request a documented Graph transfer. Same-tenant Teams restrictions and application-instance PSTN requirements apply. Treat HTTP 202 as acceptance, then observe asynchronous outcomes. Consultative transfer requires its own supported call topology. Release media only when the call lifecycle permits it; retain context and a failure path if the handoff does not complete. Reuse Python AI engines, YAML definitions/tools, and storage behind an explicit new bridge. Reuse is a design goal, not current channel compatibility. Add Entra app/calling bot, application instance, Graph consent, Azure Windows/.NET media hosts, per-call affinity, callbacks, and a custom duplex/control bridge. Remove from this path ACS Call Automation, ACS Event Grid integration, ACS media framing, and ACS-number identity. Audit email/SMS separately before claiming complete ACS removal. Graph supports PSTN origination, inbound, and transfer scenarios. Follow the application-instance/number prerequisites, rather than assuming every identity can call any destination. The transfer API notes a same-tenant Teams scope and PSTN transfer only for application instances. Bot number management · Answer · Transfer and asynchronous response . REST v1.0 is not the media platform's release label. The application-hosted media article still calls the real-time media platform developer preview. sections.title: 04  SIP gateway + Teams Direct Routing
sections.text: Proposed Gateway vendor and interface not selected. License checklist Keep Python behind a programmable SIP/contact-center gateway. The gateway owns call control and duplex audio; a certified SBC supplies Teams connectivity. Connect model · Direct Routing prerequisites . Swap: ACS control/media → vendor gateway. Add: a channel bridge for its duplex audio contract. See the component mapping . Not sufficient: a certified SBC alone is not an AI media API, and does not certify the whole voice-agent solution. SIP architecture, call flows & vendor transfer contract Illustrative topology, not a selected vendor design. SIP/TLS is signaling; RTP/SRTP is media (Teams-side media uses SRTP). The gateway must anchor the required audio and expose a confirmed duplex interface. Media bypass can change the actual media route. Text equivalent & all flow steps Inbound call The configured carrier/SBC/Teams route sends an incoming call to the chosen gateway. The exact entry route is a vendor design decision. The gateway answers using its documented SIP/call-control interface; the SBC does not supply a generic answer API to Python. The gateway anchors RTP/SRTP and simultaneously receives/injects audio through its confirmed app interface. A new channel bridge maps formats, pacing, barge-in, and lifecycle into the retained engine, tools, and state. Outbound call Python requests origination through the selected gateway's documented control contract, not through Teams Direct Routing alone. The gateway/SBC uses the authorized carrier or Teams route and permitted caller identity. Routing and commercial arrangements must be confirmed. Track provisional, answered, failed, and disconnected states through the vendor's event contract. After answer, the gateway bridges two-way audio. A one-way recording feed cannot serve this architecture. Human handoff Choose blind or consultative transfer, a validated destination, and a least-data context handoff contract. Invoke the vendor-supported transfer flow. Validate SIP REFER/NOTIFY direction and any new INVITE legs for this topology. Observe signaling and final call outcomes. REFER acceptance, ringing, and human answer are different milestones. Retain or recover media on failure and close only the correct legs. Validate media-bypass and failure-recovery behavior explicitly. Reuse Python/Linux hosting, AI engines and business definitions, tools, and state behind a purpose-built channel bridge. Add Selected gateway/control service, confirmed duplex API, certified SBC, carrier/Teams routing, DNS/certificates/networking, monitoring, and vendor operations. Remove from this path ACS control, callbacks/Event Grid, ACS framing, and ACS number dependency. The gateway replaces these responsibilities; they do not disappear. No invented endpoint: this guide deliberately does not name a generic wss:// SIP media URL. Transport, authentication, codecs, pacing, interruption, concurrency, and commercial rights remain vendor-dependent and unconfirmed . Transfer direction matters. Microsoft's Direct Routing article describes the Teams SIP proxy either handling a transfer locally with a new INVITE, or sending REFER to the SBC , which handles a new INVITE using the provided context. SBC NOTIFY support is required; SBC REFER handling is required for the documented media-bypass transfer case. This is not a guarantee that an arbitrary bot-originated REFER into Teams will work. Validate REFER-TO/REFERRED-BY, Replaces behavior, and blind/consultative flows with the SBC/gateway vendor. Official SIP transfer contract . A certified SBC establishes the Direct Routing device boundary, not certification of the entire voice-agent solution. Agree which party owns carrier incidents, Teams routing, gateway media, and the AI runtime. Contact-center solution certification .

sections.title: 05  Managed Teams Phone Agent / Copilot Studio
sections.text: Preview Replace the conversational runtime, not just the phone provider. Teams Phone Agent licenses · Copilot Studio licenses Move the conversation into a managed product. The native setup lists no custom ACS resource or PCM bridge to this accelerator; Microsoft's internal stack is undisclosed. Teams Phone Agent · Direct-dial Copilot Studio . Swap: custom telephony and conversation runtime → managed product. Prompts and tools need migration, not just a new transport. See the component mapping . Fit gate: the Copilot Teams channel is basic-voice only, not real-time, with classic orchestration and tenant enablement. Do not assume Cascade/VoiceLive or outbound-automation parity. Channel limits . Managed architecture, call flows & preview boundaries A Teams RA routes to a product-hosted agent. The custom accelerator voice loop is not in this path; prompts, tools, knowledge, and handoff behavior must be mapped to the chosen product's supported features. Text equivalent & all flow steps Inbound call A configured Teams service number and AI Agent resource account route the call to the enabled product/channel. Teams Phone Agent or the supported Copilot Studio voice channel runs the conversation in the managed runtime. The managed agent uses its configured knowledge and allowed tools. Existing YAML/toolstore definitions do not automatically become product assets. This path has no documented custom PCM bridge to Cascade or VoiceLive. Evaluate the supported product experience instead. Outbound automation boundary The cited native setup is not documentation for arbitrary app-originated outbound calls or SIP automation. Do not reinterpret a product's call-transfer tool as a generic create_call API for this accelerator. Confirm a separately documented product capability before designing proactive outbound scenarios. No outbound call is animated here because no such integration is established. Human handoff Configure only destinations and transfer behavior supported by the selected managed product. The managed agent invokes its supported transfer workflow through Teams telephony. Observe product outcomes and handle unsuccessful routing using the product's supported fallbacks, not assumed ACS/Graph hooks. Any human-facing summary or business context needs a supported connector and appropriate permissions; it is not implied by the call transfer. Carry forward Business requirements, reviewed prompts, knowledge, and allowed tools as migration inputs, not drop-in YAML/runtime reuse. Add Product eligibility, tenant/channel enablement, licensed RA/number configuration, managed agent configuration, governance, and product-specific testing. Replace This application's telephony integration and conversational runtime. External business services may be connected only through supported product mechanisms. Basic voice is not real-time channel parity. The linked Copilot Studio Teams channel supports basic voice agents only ; real-time voice agents are explicitly unsupported. It calls for classic orchestration (not generative orchestration), tenant enablement by Microsoft, and Copilot Studio tenant/user licensing. Do not use Dynamics 365 real-time voice-agent documentation as proof of Teams channel support. Teams channel prerequisites and limitations · Separate Dynamics 365 real-time offering . Teams Phone Agent remains Frontier Public Preview ; direct-dial Copilot Studio is also preview. Native RA transfer, tools, and recording features have their own boundaries. These are not GA replacements with automatic parity for Cascade, VoiceLive, arbitrary outbound calls, or SIP automation. Product status and limitations .

sections.title: Human handoff: acceptance is not completion
sections.text: Every path needs an observed outcome and a failure fallback. A YAML agent handoff changes the AI persona, not the telephone call. Context is a separate data path. A summary, authentication state, transcript, and CRM reference do not automatically travel with a phone call.
